recipes.name: Sweet and Savory Kale
ingredients_raw: 4 cups stemmed, torn and rinsed kale

steps.text: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion and garlic; cook and stir until onion softens and turns translucent, about 5 minutes. Add chicken broth, sugar, mustard, and vinegar; bring to a boil over high heat. Stir in kale; cook, covered, until wilted, about 5 minutes.
Add dried cranberries; boil, uncovered, until liquid reduces by about half and cranberries soften, about 15 minutes. Season with salt and black pepper. Sprinkle with sliced almonds before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Sweet and Savory Kale
raw_recipe.description: This flavorful sweet and savory braised kale recipe includes a combo of sweet and tangy ingredients, for a colorful, healthy, and nutritious side dish.

review.reviewBody:
Well, I have to admit that it was very good. I have never had kale, or any other "southern" type of green. They used to sound kinda gross to me. But, my CSA box sent me a bunch of kale and I wanted to try it one time, to see if I truly did not like it or not. I wanted a simple recipe. This recipe fit the bill perfectly, and it tasted really good too.
Way to go Surja! We will be making this again. Only changes will be halving the sugar in half and greatly increasing the dried cranberries. 
Very easy and quick to make. Make sure the Kale is dried off very well.

Great alternative to caldo verde. I saw on PBS that kale has more micronutrients than any other vegetable; so we need more of these tasty recipes using kale. I used 2 tsp of honey in place of the sugar and also used 1/3 cup dried cranberries. My cooking times were about half as long as in the recipe; I judged based on the colour of the onions and the amount of liquid reduction. To me, the cider vinegar is the key ingredient that should not be substituted; it adds the right combination of tanginess and sweetness. I also think adding a touch of heat, like chili flakes, would make it even better.

I really liked this recipe! I, too made some changes- reduced the sugar to 1 tsp (I may leave it out next time- don't think it really even needed it), left out the onion b/c I didn't have any and added extra garlic. I also followed another reviewers recommendation and reduced the liquid before adding the kale so it wasn't too mushy. I gave it 4 stars because of all the tweaking, but I did like it very much.

Delicious! My only problems were that it was too sweet and too soupy. Made it again with just the sugar on the cranberries and 1 t added sugar and about 1/3 cup broth and simmered it covered and I liked it much better. Keeper!

I thought this was delicious, but with my experience cooking Kale I did add a couple of things, and I changed the chicken stock to vegetable stock for a vegetarian dish. I added some red chili flakes to the onion and garlic, and then grated fresh nutmeg after adding the Kale. I think Kale always needs some citrus, so I squeezed fresh orange juice at the end. I'll definitely make this again!

Hands down the most delicious kale recipe EVER!!! However, would just like to note that the olive oil is completely unnecessary- Bring the chicken broth to a boil then throw in the chopped onions- they will cook while it boils, no need to cook separately in oil. Then mix in the other ingredients. I substitute stevia for the sugar to save on calories too. When you cut out the olive oil and sugar this brings this recipe down to about 80 calories per serving!

Kale is a superfood* but most nutrients are destroyed in this cooking method. "Healthy steam" the Kale and add at the very end. It turns out chewier but if you're going to eat it, you might as well get the most out of it. *Kale is one of the healthiest vegetables around and one way to be sure to enjoy the maximum nutrition and flavor from kale is to cook it properly. It's recommended to Healthy Steam kale for 5 minutes. To ensure quick and even cooking cut the leaves into 1/2" slices and the stems into 1/4" lengths. Let them sit for at least 5 minutes to enhance their health-promoting qualities before steaming.
I reduce the sugar to 1 tablespoon, and took it uptown subbing balsamic for cider vinegar and pine nuts for almonds.
Delicious! I substituted maple syrup for white sugar and balsamic vinegar for cider vinegar.

I loved this, I took others advice and only used 1 cup of broth and did not add any sugar, it was sweet enough. I've made it 3 times and used dried cranberries, tart cherries, and prunes, so any dried fruit will work. Also, there is no way this makes 6 servings, more like 3 small or 2 large.

I made the full recipe, strained most of the remaining liquid and divided it into thirds to eat as 3 lunches instead of a side. Used all measurements exactly. Definitely enough Craisins. Used the following subs for health or convenience: low sodium chicken broth, white vinegar, 50% less sugar Craisins. I only added almonds just before eating (2 Tbsp). Followed cooking directions exactly. The vinegar could be slightly less. This was a great way to get kale into my diet and it fills you up. Accompanied it with a slice of wheat toast. I'm watching calories via MyFitnessPal, so divided into thirds with all substitutions, it's about 230 calories and 288 with a slice of bread.
Love Love Love it!!! Tastes like something from a restaurant

I doubled the recipe and used approximately 2 tablespoons of honey instead of sugar. It was delicious as is for a regular family dinner, but I would use the almonds and cranberries to make it prettier for company.

Very good! I will be making kale more often now.
Great flavor. I toasted the almonds.
Delicious! Will make this again.

Oh my! This was definitely I great switch up from how I normally make kale.... this will become a staple in my house now. If you like sweet and tanginess of sweet and sour chicken, you are going to love this.
I have made this several times, it's my go-to kale recipe. It does a good job of tapering the strong taste of kale.
agree - first time making kale & this is good. halved sugar as advised...used whole mustard Dijon.
